terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == -1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * (1 + ep_dec) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (1 + ep_dec) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("action", -1) == 2) * (tv("reward", -1) == 0) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (1 + ep_dec)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 40 is saturated by phase (about +0.9 at D1, -1 at GO, +1 at D2); timing explains R^2 0.99, and almost all residual variance is at D1 (GO and D2 residuals are under 0.01). At D1 the value is pushed down by an unrewarded a2 previous trial, most strongly a2 S2 u (common, unrewarded; about -0.3). It goes down further when the trial before was also an unrewarded a2 (streaks of a2 losses can push it below 0). These drops get bigger later in the episode: scaling them by (1 + episode decile) took dev R^2 from 0.48 to 0.54. A previous reward raises it (+0.11), and reaching S2 on the previous trial lowers it (-0.09). Policy, value and hidden good state add little. Observed-only terms; dev R^2 beyond timing 0.537, against a profile ceiling of all 0.55 / all observed 0.53.

issues: Reproduced the score: the claimed terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.546. Without the (1+ep_dec) scaling they give 0.483, so the claim that the drops grow later in the episode holds.

There is one systematic but small miss. At D1 after 'a1 S1 u' the terms under-predict by +0.089, and also by +0.040 after a1 S2 r and +0.029 after a1 S2 u. The terms treat any unrewarded trial as baseline, but after a1 trials the value stays high whether or not the trial was rewarded. Adding (phase==D1)*(prev_action==1) (weight +0.042) raises test R^2 to 0.560 and shrinks the a1 S1 u miss to +0.050. So the label's '+0.11 for a previous reward' partly stands in for 'the previous trial was a1'.

The streak drop does not depend on the state reached. An a2 S1 u after an earlier a2 loss gets about the same extra drop as an a2 S2 u after an a2 loss (weights -0.014 vs -0.011 per (1+ep_dec)). The worst-fit windows that go below 0 include a2 S1R u runs. 'Especially a2 S2 u' is true only for the single previous trial (a2 S2 u residual -0.31 vs a2 S1 u -0.05).

The ceiling is low. The 'all' additive ceiling is 0.55, and nothing pushed test R^2 past about 0.56: not policy logit or value at D1 (0.552), not the future action (0.558), not the hidden good state (0.546). About 44% of the D1 residual variance remains unexplained by any available cue. It most likely reflects a2-loss history older than the 5-trial window. The explanation reports this ceiling honestly, so it is not an overclaim, but 'explained' rests on 99% of a ceiling that is itself only 0.55.
With the a1 term added, no large error class is left in misses: per-phase mean errors are within 0.001, and GO and D2 residuals are under 0.01, as claimed.
